body:
Jeff Bromkey account — scheduling fit
Jeff's facility has a messy schedule to model: rentable golf-sim bays (bookable without a coach), regular strength sessions, and open gym — effectively appointment-style, not class-style.
OS's current schedule build-out is optimized for a simple gym (~8 classes/day → 30–45 min to set the whole week, then set forever). It breaks down with many moving parts like Jeff's.
Member-booked appointments is the real fix for most of Jeff's problems: e.g. golf bays as an appointment (12–12, 30/60-min chunks); coaching sessions are a textbook fit.
Open wrinkle: golf-sim bays technically require an instructor → workaround: a "dummy user" booked into the session (same mechanic as a PT appointment, minus a real person).
Timeline: member-booked appointments kicks off next week, targeting mid-August completion. Plan is to bridge Jeff ~6–7 weeks on the promise it fixes this wholesale. Judged low churn risk (Jeff, the payer, is easygoing); a ~6-week discount is the fallback only if they push back.

Schedule build-out — "copy session" feature
Recurring request: build one day, copy it across the week — and copy within a day. Trent + Tophie to look at it; likely need both (within-day and across-week) since one's useless without the other.
Flagged as a next-cycle investigation, not now.
Design principle Trent pushed on the collaborator: draw the line between software doing the work and helping the user get work done. Too many edit choices → users get lost and can't tell what they changed. "If it's complicated to explain, it's probably complicated to use." Homework: think it through as the actual user workflow / field-of-vision, not the dev effort.

Onboarding audit / customer interviews
Trent wants to run the onboarding audit (interview customers on what went wrong) — but only once the question set is buttoned-up. Risk to avoid: it devolves into a gripe session or a feature-request call ("this isn't a feature call"). Keep feedback pointed.
Sequence: Trent drafts questions → circle up with collaborator to make them robust/exhaustive → vet on Andrea first (new, easy, low stakes) → then Brie.
(Already tracked as an open loop: "trent to create outline of interview questions.")

Claude "Onboarding Assistant" (the blueprint tool)
Problem it targets: onboarding is inherently heavy (moving payments, memberships) and not truly self-service unless you're software-savvy.
Concept: run a structured "nuts to screws" interview when a customer buys / is about to buy → feed the transcript into the Claude project → it emits an OS blueprint: the class categories, classes, memberships mapped to those classes, and schedule items that account needs. Hand to the customer or a CSM. It never builds anything — it just translates the customer's business into OS terms.
Currently testing internally (not sending to customers yet).
Trent walked the current schema and asked "what's missing." Sections: Categories (classes) & Appointments; Schedule item types (class/appointment/workshop) + how to decide class vs. appointment (publicly-booked-but-appointment → still a class); Products (memberships/packages, retail, promo); Staff profiles → permission levels (admin vs. front desk, e.g. Quinn needs booking but not reporting); Studio settings (rooms, cancellation policy, booking window, Stripe connected, branding — branding optional); Output spec.
Two common setup mistakes baked in as call-outs: (1) category collapse — everything in one category; (2) the opposite — many categories but a membership granted access to only one (Brie hit this). Rule added: every membership in the blueprint must list which categories it needs, with a note on why.
Gaps surfaced in the room: something Trent "completely forgot about" (membership-related); linking OS to a customer's website (noted as out-of-scope for this doc for now).
(Related existing open loop: "trent to add waiver handling to claude assisted onboarding.")

In-platform info call-outs (tooltips)
Add info call-outs (ⓘ) next to fields — especially membership/billing — explaining what they mean and their downstream effect (e.g. payment due date vs. membership start date; a one-off "billed 6 days late this cycle, back to the 1st next time" case).
Model it on the payment portal's dynamic readout ("14-day trial, then charged on day 14, every X days for X cycles") — a plain-language dynamic summary.
Add a call-out on the discount line flagging "one-time discount" (gets missed a lot).
Assessed as a fast-twitch build: if it's just on-hover copy, it changes no behavior.

Logistics
Trent OOO Thu/Fri (New Orleans conference — reachable for fires) and all next week except Mon AM (Jake in town).

Bug/build triage: the Stripe Connect onboarding flow is too manual and won't scale, so it's getting a super-admin gate; plus an 'insufficient credits' member-facing modal rewrite (FastTwitch) and a mobile pricing-link bug. Active speakers were Trent, Quinn, Elvis, and Brian; James was present but silent and Luke Green joined at the very end.

Stripe re-auth: Trent re-pinged the Stripe bug ticket. Tyler noted the current fix won't help his specific situation but may help later — status only, not a commitment. Trent flagged the whole re-auth flow as more painful than expected (too many manual steps; he has to remember the custom support request after the customer connects), and with 3 signups in the last 10 days it will break at scale. Resolution: gate the Connect button behind a super-admin toggle (see decisions).

Insufficient-credits modal: two related member problems — members double-buy memberships when out of credits, and owners field confused 'I'm out of credits' questions. Fix is to make the modal clearer/dynamic (e.g. 'you've used all your credits; your next booking window starts X'). Only hard part is fetching the next period (needs backend); simple copy could go via Cooksey. Scoped as FastTwitch.

FYI / context (not tasks): Non-Stripe payment support is 'very' hard — OS is payment-agnostic by design (rebuilt that way) but every flow needs building; endgame is switching processors to skim the ~2.5% once volume grows, tied to the Intermountain Health experiment and a possible Sanford pitch. ACH is exploratory — Stripe can accept ACH but OS isn't set up for it (it does iBAN/SEPA-style payments); interest is mostly Australian/international; Trent is fine eating the ~3% card fees for now. Quinn's stray ticket from yesterday is already under review.
